tasks.title: Geometry Instancing for Tulip and Sunflower Fields
tasks.description: Replace individual Mesh objects for tulips and sunflowers with InstancedMesh to reduce draw calls and improve rendering performance. This is particularly beneficial for mobile devices. Maintain individual positioning and animation capabilities through instance matrix updates. Must maintain visual fidelity while reducing GPU overhead.
tasks.testingStrategy:
- Unit tests: Test instancing math and matrix updates in isolation
- Integration tests: Verify that instanced flowers render correctly in the scene, maintain proper positioning, and animate as expected
- Performance benchmark tests: Measure FPS improvement before and after implementation, targeting >10% FPS gain on mid-range mobile devices
- Visual regression tests: Ensure instanced flowers appear visually identical to original implementation (same shapes, colors, animations)
- Acceptance criteria: Draw call count reduced by 50%+ for flower elements; FPS improvement measurable on test devices; visual output matches original within acceptable tolerance; all existing flower-related functionality preserved

tasks.title: Seasons.json Schema Validation in validate-content.js
tasks.description:
The seasons.json data file (consumed by the seasonal transitions feature, idea-037) currently has no validation in validate-content.js — the 560-line validator covers siteData.json and content.json structure but completely misses seasons.json. A malformed seasons entry (wrong month range, invalid color scheme key, missing required fields) would cause silent runtime failures in the seasonal theme rotation.

Scope:
- Add validateSeasons() function to validate-content.js
- Validate: 4 season keys (spring, summer, autumn, winter), each with months array (numbers 1-12), colorSchemeWeights (all 5 scheme keys present, values >= 1), flowerEmphasis enum, skyToneShift RGB ranges, particleEffect string, factThemeWeights (all theme keys present, values >= 1)
- Add 6+ test fixtures in tests/fixtures/content-validation/ (valid + various malformed)
- Wire into the validate-content.sh script pipeline
tasks.testingStrategy:
- Unit tests: Add tests/unit/validate-seasons.test.js with fixtures for valid seasons.json, invalid month values (0, 13), missing color scheme keys, negative weights, unknown season key. Each fixture tests a specific validation rule.
- Integration tests: Run the full validate-content.sh script against both valid and malformed seasons fixtures; verify correct exit codes (0 for valid, 1 for invalid).
- Acceptance criteria: All existing 38 validate-content tests still pass; new season validation catches all defined error types; validate-content.sh exits non-zero on malformed seasons.json; error messages are actionable (specify which season/field failed).

tasks.title: Dead Shader Code Cleanup in scene-shaders.js
tasks.description:
The scene-shaders.js module still exports four shader strings (vgVS, vgFS, glitchVS, glitchFS) that were part of the post-processing pipeline removed in the 2026-05-20 refactoring. These exports are no longer imported by scene-manager.js or any other module — they are dead code consuming ~2.5KB. This cleanup removes the unused exports, consolidates the remaining active shaders (starVS, starFS, wave uniforms) with JSDoc annotations, and adds a brief comment documenting why the removed shaders existed historically.

Also audit: verify no other public/js/scene/ modules import the removed exports.
tasks.testingStrategy:
- Unit tests: After removal, verify no module in public/js/ imports vgVS, vgFS, glitchVS, or glitchFS (AST/grep check).
- Integration tests: Run npm run build and verify build succeeds with zero errors.
- Acceptance criteria: scene-shaders.js exports only active shader strings; build succeeds; bundle size reduced by ~2.5KB; no import errors in any scene module; remaining shader exports unchanged and functional.

tasks.title: Unit Tests for Scene Utility Functions (scene-utils.js)
tasks.description:
The scene-utils.js module exports pure functions (getMoonPhase, getMoonPhaseName, getMoonEmoji, getMoonIllumination, lerp, clamp, etc.) that are completely untested. These are ideal unit-test candidates: they have no DOM/Three.js dependencies and can be validated with precise expected values including known astronomical new moon dates and phase boundary conditions.

Scope:
- Create tests/unit/scene-utils.test.js
- Test getMoonPhase() against known historical new moon dates (e.g., 2026-01-19, 2026-02-17)
- Test getMoonPhaseName() boundary values (exact 0.0625, 0.1875, etc.)
- Test getMoonEmoji() returns correct Unicode for each phase
- Test lerp/clamp utility math functions
tasks.testingStrategy:
- Unit tests: Create tests/unit/scene-utils.test.js with known-value tests for getMoonPhase() using fixed dates (not 'new Date()'). Test phase name boundaries with exact fraction values. Test helper math functions (lerp, clamp, etc.) with edge cases.
- Integration tests: Verify that scene-utils functions produce values consistent with what scene-init.js expects (phase fraction 0-1 range, emoji string format).
- Acceptance criteria: All new tests pass; getMoonPhase accuracy within 1 day of known astronomical data; 100% branch coverage for getMoonPhaseName(); no regressions in existing validate-content test suite.
tasks.reviewNotes: Reviewed 2026-06-08 03:00 — PASS. 52 unit tests for scene-utils.js covering getMoonPhase (known astronomical dates, range validation, leap years, year boundaries), getMoonPhaseName (all 8 boundary values, 100% branch coverage), getMoonEmoji (8 distinct emojis, boundary alignment), _seededRand (determinism, range, seed divergence), and integration tests. All 52 tests pass. Build succeeds. Site live (HTTP 200). Zero scene-init.js changes. Clean JSDoc comments.

ideas.title: Offline PWA Shell — Service Worker Cache

The sw.js uses a versioned cache name (atrija-vX) so future deploys bust the cache. Shows a subtle 'offline-ready' toast on first successful cache. Total added code: ~60 lines SW + ~15 lines registration.

ideas.title: Keyboard Shortcuts Help Overlay
ideas.description: Press '?' anywhere on the site to open a modal overlay listing all available keyboard shortcuts: '/' for content search, Tab/Shift+Tab for section navigation, Space/Enter for interactive elements, and Escape to dismiss. The modal is styled in the impressionist dark theme with gold accent borders. Includes a brief 'Keyboard Navigation' section explaining the site's keyboard-first design. Implemented as a standalone public/js/keyboard-help.js module with a focus-trap inside the modal for accessibility. Zero scene-init.js changes. Fills a clear UX gap: the site has multiple keyboard-driven features but zero discoverability for them.

ideas.title: Light Mode — prefers-color-scheme Support
ideas.description: Respect the user's OS-level color scheme preference by providing a light/cream impressionist palette activated via @media (prefers-color-scheme: light). The light mode uses warm cream (#faf6f0) backgrounds, dark brown (#2a1f14) text, and softened gold accents — evoking sunlit canvas rather than night sky. All color values are CSS custom property overrides under the media query, so zero JS is required. The existing 3D scene remains unchanged (it's a dark sky scene). Text content, cards, navigation, and the loader all adapt. Enhances accessibility for users who experience eye strain in dark environments or simply prefer light themes.

ideas.title: Content JSON Schema Validation
ideas.description: Add runtime validation for siteData.json and content.json using lightweight manual validators to catch malformed content before it breaks the build or renders broken sections. Implemented as a standalone src/content/validate-content.js module with scripts/validate-content.sh CI check.
